heic-v-jpg.title: iPhone photos to JPG: HEIC online with no server upload
heic-v-jpg.description: Free HEIC/HEIF to JPG converter in the browser. Open iPhone photos on Windows and in forms — no cloud and no apps.
heic-v-jpg.lead: Shot on iPhone — but the file won’t open on a PC or in a form? Convert HEIC/HEIF to JPG locally, with no cloud and no sign-up.
body: The iPhone camera writes HEIC by default (sometimes HEIF). Windows, many websites, printers, and email attachments expect plain JPG — so “iPhone photos” often won’t open on a computer.
How to use: pick one or more .heic/.heif → conversion to JPG runs in the browser → download the file or a ZIP. Adjust quality and long edge to match a form limit.
PixLocal never uploads the shot to a server — unlike typical cloud converters. HEIC decoding and JPEG saving stay on the device; you can shrink the file before sending.

faq.q: How do I open an iPhone photo on Windows?
faq.a: Transfer the HEIC to your PC and convert it here to JPG — no codecs or apps to install. The file doesn’t go to the cloud: processing is browser-only.

faq.q: How is HEIC different from JPG?
faq.a: HEIC is more compact and newer (iPhone camera standard); JPG is the universal format for Windows, websites, and printing. Conversion is for compatibility.

faq.q: Does the photo go to a server?
faq.a: No. HEIC decoding and JPG saving run in the browser. Check the Network tab: the image body is not sent.
When re-encoding via Canvas, some EXIF may be lost. Keep the original HEIC for important archives.

faq.q: Why is JPG sometimes larger than HEIC?
faq.a: HEIC is more efficient than JPEG. We automatically lower quality and cap the side (default 2560 px) so the file gets lighter. Reduce quality or max side if needed.

faq.q: Can I convert several files at once?
faq.a: Yes — select a batch of HEIC and download a ZIP of JPGs, or share individual frames to Photos via Share.

webp-v-jpg.title: WebP to JPG online with no server upload
webp-v-jpg.description: Free WebP to JPG converter locally in the browser. Files never go to the cloud.
webp-v-jpg.lead: Open a downloaded WebP in any editor: convert to JPG locally on your device.
body: WebP is common on websites and in messengers. If an editor, printer, or Windows form only opens JPG — re-encode the file here.
Decoding and JPEG saving run in the browser: the source is never uploaded. You can cap the long edge so the attachment doesn’t balloon.
Batch: several WebP at once, then ZIP or Share on iPhone. Use the quality slider when you need a sharpness-vs-size tradeoff.

faq.q: Why is JPG heavier than WebP?
faq.a: WebP is usually more efficient. JPG is for compatibility, not for a smaller file.
No: JPG gets a single frame. For a clip, keep the original WebP or convert to video.

png-v-jpg.title: PNG to JPG online
png-v-jpg.description: Free PNG to JPG converter online, locally in the browser.
png-v-jpg.lead: Convert PNG to JPG and cut file size a lot for the web and messengers.
body: PNG is great for graphics, screenshots, and transparency, but often overkill for photos: JPG of the same scene can be many times smaller.
Transparent areas become a light Canvas background when saved as JPG — check the preview if the alpha channel matters.
Handy before email, a CMS, or a marketplace where PNG hits a size limit. You can lower quality and max side further.

faq.a: Stay on PNG or pick WebP in the main compressor on the home page.

faq.q: Why does a screenshot look soft?
faq.a: JPEG handles fine text poorly. Raise quality toward 90% or keep PNG/WebP for UI.

faq.q: Can I do a batch at once?
faq.a: Yes — select several PNGs and download a ZIP of JPGs.

jpg-v-png.title: JPG to PNG online
jpg-v-png.description: JPG to PNG converter online in the browser with no sign-up.
jpg-v-png.lead: Convert JPEG to PNG locally when you need PNG for further editing.
body: JPG→PNG conversion does not restore detail already lost to JPEG. But you can edit further without new “JPEG generation” artifacts.
The PNG will be noticeably heavier than the source — normal for a lossless format. If size is the goal, prefer WebP or recompress JPG.
Processing is local: handy when a template, print shop, or stock asks for PNG specifically.

faq.a: Often yes: lossless PNG is usually heavier than JPEG.
No. JPEG has no alpha channel, so the PNG will be opaque. Transparency must be added separately.

faq.q: Why do this if PNG is heavier?
faq.a: When the next step is an editor or print workflow that needs PNG, not kilobyte savings.

jpg-v-webp.title: JPG to WebP online
jpg-v-webp.description: JPG to WebP converter for websites — locally in the browser.
jpg-v-webp.lead: Prep images for fast pages: JPG → WebP with no cloud.
body: WebP on a site is usually lighter than JPEG at similar looks — fewer bytes for LCP and mobile data.
PixLocal encodes WebP in the browser: source JPGs never go to a server. Set quality and, if needed, cap the side.
Keep a JPG fallback in your markup for older clients: the converter gives you a modern file — it doesn’t mean every browser forgot JPEG.

faq.a: Modern ones do. Keep a JPG fallback for older clients.

faq.q: Is it good for product photos?
faq.a: Yes — quality 75–85% is usually enough. Check the preview on fine text and gradients.
Yes — upload several JPGs and download a ZIP of WebP.

png-v-webp.title: PNG to WebP online
png-v-webp.description: Free PNG to WebP converter online in the browser.
png-v-webp.lead: Compress PNG to WebP locally — great for landings and product cards.
body: WebP is often lighter than PNG at a similar look — especially photos and soft gradients. For flat-color icons the gain is smaller; check the preview.
WebP supports transparency: a logo on a transparent background usually survives conversion, but check anti-aliased edges.
Done locally, with no cloud queue. If you need maximum lossless PNG, this mode is not a substitute for oxipng/pngquant.

faq.a: WebP supports an alpha channel; the result depends on the browser encoder. Check object edges in the preview.
Small UI, pixel art, text screenshots — if WebP looks mushy. Then resize PNG without changing format.

faq.q: Is this for an online store?
faq.a: Yes: cards and banners often shrink without a visible hit. Don’t replace everything wholesale without spot-checking.

webp-v-png.title: WebP to PNG online
webp-v-png.description: WebP to PNG converter online, processed in the browser.
webp-v-png.lead: Need PNG from WebP — convert locally and download the result.
body: You need PNG because Photoshop, a print shop, or a form won’t take WebP — re-encode locally and download the file.
Lossless PNG is almost always heavier than the source WebP. If size is the goal, stay on WebP or go to JPG without transparency.
Animated WebP collapses to a single frame. This tool is not for clips.

faq.a: Usually yes — lossless PNG weighs more than WebP.
If the WebP had an alpha channel, PNG keeps it. Opaque WebP yields opaque PNG.

faq.q: Why is there one image when the source “blinked”?
faq.a: Animation is not transferred. Export video or GIF from an editor, not through this converter.

izmenit-razmer.title: Resize photos online
izmenit-razmer.description: Reduce photo resolution online — resize the long edge in the browser.
izmenit-razmer.lead: Cap the long edge in pixels and shrink file size if needed.
body: Resizing the long edge is a quick way to meet social/CMS limits and speed up pages: fewer pixels mean less weight even at the same JPEG quality.
Set a max on the longer side (default 1920 px); proportions stay. No need to calculate the short side.
Upscaling is technically possible, but sharpness won’t appear: the tool is built for reducing. Files never leave the device.

faq.a: Technically yes, but quality won’t improve. The tool is meant for reducing.
Yes — resize follows the longer side, so the aspect ratio stays intact.

faq.q: How else can I shrink size?
faq.a: After resize, lower JPEG/WebP quality or set a KB target on the home page / “to 100 KB” page.

szhat-do-100kb.title: Compress a photo to 100 KB online without the cloud
szhat-do-100kb.description: Compress an image to 100 KB locally in the browser — no server upload. Handy for forms and attachments.
szhat-do-100kb.lead: Fit a file under a form or attachment limit — 100 KB target, processed locally.
body: A 100 KB limit is common on government forms, job applications, email attachments, and older forums. The tool tunes JPEG/WebP quality and resolution until weight approaches the target.
By default the long edge is up to 1600 px and the target is 100 KB. If the frame is noisy or very detailed, drop the side to 1280 or 1024 px and recalculate.
Everything runs in the browser — a passport scan or form photo doesn’t go to someone else’s cloud. Exactly 102400 bytes isn’t always possible: the goal is “fit”, not bit-for-bit.

faq.q: Is it safe to compress documents?
faq.a: File contents are not sent to the PixLocal server. Processing is browser-only. Google Analytics may count button clicks, not file names or pixels.

faq.q: Do I always get exactly 100 KB?
faq.a: Not always — it depends on the frame. You can also lower the max side in pixels.

faq.q: Why does the photo look soft?
faq.a: To fit 100 KB you must trade detail. Resize first, then quality: that usually looks livelier than only a very low JPEG.

faq.q: Does PNG also compress to 100 KB?
faq.a: More often via JPG or WebP. Pure lossless PNG under 100 KB for photos is almost unrealistic.

szhat-png.title: Compress PNG online with no server upload
szhat-png.description: Compress PNG locally in the browser for free — the file never goes to the cloud.
szhat-png.lead: Shrink PNG size: re-encode to WebP/JPG or keep PNG with a resize.
body: A browser PNG encoder doesn’t do heavy lossless like pngquant or oxipng. If you don’t need transparency, WebP or JPG shrinks far more.
For text screenshots try WebP first: often lighter than PNG and more readable than harsh JPEG. Check logo alpha edges.
Batch PNG → ZIP on the device, no sign-up. If the file barely changed — switch output format instead of twisting the PNG slider.

faq.q: Why did the PNG barely shrink?
faq.a: Lossless PNG is limited. Switch the output format to WebP or JPG.
Aim for WebP. JPG kills transparency with a light fill.
No: there’s no cloud lossless here. But the file never leaves your computer. For icon archives, CLI optimizers are still stronger.

szhat-jpg.description: Compress JPEG locally in the browser for free — no cloud and no sign-up.
szhat-jpg.lead: Recompress JPEG with quality and size-target control — all in the browser.
body: Recompressing JPEG adds artifacts: start around 70–85% and watch the preview instead of jumping to the minimum.
Size drops most when you also resize the long edge (e.g. 1920 or 1600 px). Quality alone on a 12-megapixel frame helps less.
Several JPGs at once, ZIP at the end. Sources stay with you — handy before a site, listing, or email.

faq.a: Yes — upload several JPGs and download a ZIP.
For the web and messengers it’s usually enough. For print or archives keep the original and don’t recompress repeatedly.

faq.q: Why is the file a bit larger after compression?
faq.a: Rarely, if the source was already very light. Lower the side or quality and hit Recalculate.
